walkthroughs.body_html:
Decision Making to Improve Financial Performance — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Decision Making to Improve Financial Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Decision Making to Improve Financial Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Modigliani and Miller's irrelevance theorem was published in:

options: Annual cost calculation
Cost of capital
Capital ceiling
Credit cycle

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.

Competitive rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of suppliers, bargaining power of buyers — together determining industry attractiveness and potential profitability.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Porter's Five Forces are five business strategies a firm should choose between.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
